title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Trump confirmed Monday's US strike on Qeshm Island as a 'minor attack', and the queue of ships stuck in the Strait and Gulf grew to 158 even as oil fell on hopes of a deal. There is still no Hormuz agreement, so sea lanes stay shut while air capacity into Dubai slowly returns.

stories.headline: Trump calls Qeshm strike a 'minor attack'; ship struck off Oman kills one crew member
body: Trump confirmed the US strike on Iran after explosions on Qeshm Island, calling it a 'minor attack' on an anti-aircraft facility. US officials told CBS the strike followed IRGC fire at an American aircraft. Trump also raised a possible strike on the Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site; no attack has been confirmed.

New since yesterday: the Indian-flagged vessel MSV Al Jusufi was hit off Oman by an unidentified aerial object. Oman's coast guard rescued 13 of its 14 crew; one died. Iran's navy also claims tankers hit mines east of the strait, which no maritime authority has confirmed.
stories.soWhat: Attacks have now reached shipping outside the strait, off Oman. Keep war-risk surcharges on all Gulf and Gulf of Oman sea lanes, including east coast bypass routes.

stories.headline: Oil drops 6% on deal hopes, but the ship queue grows to 158
body: Brent fell 6.4% in 24 hours to $104.46 on Tuesday morning. Iran says the strait could reopen within 48 hours if the US meets its conditions, chiefly lifting the naval blockade. Tehran says it is waiting for a US reply; no deal has been announced.
On the water nothing has changed. The strait is still effectively closed, and 158 ships were holding position in the Strait and Gulf, up from 113 the day before.
stories.soWhat: Fuel costs are easing faster than sea capacity. Pass lower fuel through on road and air, but keep sea surcharges until ships actually move.

stories.headline: BA is back in Dubai; Lufthansa slips to 25 November; long-haul gaps stretch into 2027
body: British Airways resumed daily Heathrow–Dubai flights on 3 November. Lufthansa, SWISS and Eurowings now plan to return to Dubai on 25 November, and Austrian on 12 December. Singapore Airlines has pushed its Dubai suspension to 28 February 2027, Cathay Pacific to 31 January and KLM to 27 March.

Saudi links are still patchy. Etihad's Riyadh, Jeddah and Dammam flights stay cancelled through 5 November, Emirates plans Riyadh and Dammam on 8 November, and Akasa's Riyadh flights are off until 30 November.
stories.soWhat: New: Lufthansa's restart moved to 25 November and Asian long-haul belly space stays out into 2027. Price Asia–UAE air on freighter capacity, not belly.

stories.headline: UAE cuts petrol prices for November; diesel dips 5 fils
body: Super 98 falls to Dh4.16 a litre from Dh4.40, Special 95 to Dh4.04 and E-Plus to Dh3.97. Diesel drops only slightly, to Dh4.75 from Dh4.80.
stories.soWhat: A small diesel cut gives little room on domestic road rates. Hold the fuel surcharge level and review it again for December.

stories.headline: Warehouse tenants stay put as rents climb 12.4%
body: UAE warehouse renewals rose 21.6% to a record of about 8,200 in the first half of 2026, while rents climbed another 12.4% and new contracts fell 51.8%, per Cavendish Maxwell. Industrial and logistics requirements reached 12.3 million sq ft, up 7%, as rerouted cargo pulls demand to the Northern Emirates and the east coast.
stories.soWhat: Space is tight and dear. Sell contract logistics on capacity we already hold, and price renewals to reflect market rents.

competitors.name: Emirates SkyCargo
competitors.headline: Launches 'AI Tech' product for server racks, GPUs and chips after moving 700+ tonnes in July
body: Emirates SkyCargo launched AI Tech on 3 November for AI server racks, advanced semiconductors, GPUs and manufacturing equipment, with priority loading, special handling and monitoring from its Dubai command centre. It moved more than 700 tonnes of AI infrastructure in July alone. Racks can weigh more than 3.5 tonnes. It is on track for 23 freighters by March 2027.
competitors.soWhat: Our home carrier now sells the same AI hardware lane we just launched. Position Aramex as the end-to-end partner that books SkyCargo lift and handles customs and placement on the ground.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Dangerous goods by road across five GCC markets from its DWC hub
body: FedEx now moves eligible dangerous goods by road between the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman through its Regional Economy services. It covers lab reagents, diagnostic samples, dry ice, chemicals and lithium batteries, on ADR-aligned, TIR-registered trucks from Dubai World Central. It targets healthcare, energy, hi-tech and beauty.
competitors.soWhat: With Saudi flights still patchy, FedEx is selling road for regulated freight. Check our DG road offer and price against it for healthcare and battery shippers.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Aramex Data Center Logistics goes live across the GCC, Southeast Asia, Taiwan and the US South
body: Aramex launched Data Center Logistics, live from 1 November, covering transformers, switchgear, chillers, AI racks, network gear and spare parts from factory to placement inside data halls. Hubs named include Abu Dhabi, Riyadh, Johor, Texas and Louisiana. A crated AI rack weighs about 1.75 tonnes and is worth several million dollars; crates carry shock, tilt and temperature sensors. Our latest reported result is still Q2 2026: revenue Dh1.83 billion, net profit Dh47 million.
competitors.soWhat: Emirates SkyCargo announced AI Tech the same day. Move fast to sign anchor data centre projects in Abu Dhabi and Riyadh before the lane gets crowded.

opportunities.title: AI data centre build-out
opportunities.text: Aramex Data Center Logistics is live. Target Abu Dhabi and Riyadh projects with factory-to-data-hall packages before rivals lock them in.

opportunities.title: Lower fuel on road and air
opportunities.text: Brent is down 6% and UAE petrol prices fell for November. Use it to win road and air tenders without cutting sea surcharges.

opportunities.title: Gulf road network for regulated goods
opportunities.text: Saudi flights stay patchy until at least 8 November. Push road DG and healthcare services across the GCC.

opportunities.title: Warehouse capacity we already hold
opportunities.text: Rents are up 12.4% and new contracts are scarce. Sell spare contract logistics space at market rates.

watchouts.title: Attacks spreading beyond the strait
watchouts.text: A vessel was hit off Oman and Iran claims tankers hit mines east of Hormuz. East coast bypass lanes are not risk-free.

watchouts.title: Deal hopes are not a deal
watchouts.text: Oil fell on Iran's 48-hour offer, but there is no agreement and the ship queue grew to 158.

watchouts.title: Pickaxe Mountain
watchouts.text: Trump raised a possible strike on Iran's underground nuclear site. Any strike could close airspace again.

watchouts.title: Houthi pressure on Saudi Arabia
watchouts.text: Saudi Arabia intercepted a Houthi missile aimed at its south and a drone near Mecca, a risk for Red Sea and KSA routes.

watchouts.title: Rivals crowding the AI hardware lane
watchouts.text: Emirates SkyCargo launched AI Tech the same week as our service, with its own freighters and Dubai command centre.

moves.title: Extend war-risk cover to Gulf of Oman lanes
moves.text: Apply the Gulf sea surcharge to Fujairah, Khor Fakkan and Sohar routings after the strike off Oman.

moves.title: Pass the fuel drop through on air and road only
moves.text: Review the fuel surcharge for road and air this week; leave sea surcharges unchanged until transits recover.

moves.title: Build a target list for Data Center Logistics
moves.text: List the top AI data centre projects in Abu Dhabi and Riyadh and book meetings this month.

moves.title: Partner, don't fight, SkyCargo on AI Tech
moves.text: Ask Emirates SkyCargo for AI Tech block space so we sell door-to-door with their lift.

moves.title: Benchmark our GCC DG road offer against FedEx
moves.text: Compare lanes, transit times and prices for lab samples, dry ice and lithium batteries.

moves.title: Reprice warehouse renewals
moves.text: Bring expiring contract logistics deals in line with the 12.4% rise in market rents.
